classification.difficultyReason: Form an area model from a perimeter, reconcile three metric units and interpret the interval satisfying a strict quadratic inequality.

content.prompt: A rectangle has perimeter $180\text{ mm}$. Let one side have length of $x\text{ m}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write down an expression for the area $A$ of this rectangle in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
$180\text{ mm}=0.18\text{ m}$, so the sum of two adjacent sides is $0.09\text{ m}$. The other side is $(0.09-x)\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=x(0.09-x)\text{ m}^2\\A&=(0.09x-x^2)\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What values may $x$ take if $A>20\text{ cm}^2$? Take care with the units.

answer.worked:
$20\text{ cm}^2=0.002\text{ m}^2$, and positive side lengths require $0<x<0.09$.
$$\begin{align*}x(0.09-x)&>0.002\\x^2-0.09x+0.002&<0\\(x-0.04)(x-0.05)&<0\end{align*}$$
The zeroes are $0.04$ and $0.05$. The product is positive at $x=0$, negative at $x=0.045$ and positive at $x=0.06$. Hence it is negative between the zeroes.
$$0.04<x<0.05.$$
Both endpoints are excluded because the area inequality is strict. This interval satisfies the positive-length restriction.
